generation_lock: No Part 4 item may be generated from these blueprints until status is 'Approved for Pilot' and human approval is recorded.

policy.example_policy: Generate example (0) from a family/target/keyword not used in scored slots and not used in the example of E01/E02.

batch_design_rationale.untested_families_prioritised: TF-11 Fixed expressions & collocations and TF-14 Clause & phrase restructuring were the only two families left untested after E01/E02. The Blueprint System v1.0 §10 explicitly requires them to be prioritised in the next batch. TF-11 is placed in E03 and TF-14 in E04, one each, so that neither is repeated in neighbouring exams.
batch_design_rationale.neighbour_separation: E03 draws its five remaining families from the E01 set (TF-01, TF-02, TF-05, TF-09, TF-12) and E04 from the E02 set (TF-03, TF-04, TF-06, TF-07, TF-10). No primary family is repeated between two consecutive exams anywhere in E01→E04.
batch_design_rationale.families_rested_this_batch: TF-08 Causative & service structures (used E01) and TF-13 Quantifiers, determiners & exclusivity (used E02). Both have narrow B2 target ranges and were tested recently; they should return in the next batch.
batch_design_rationale.target_structure_freshness: Every reused family carries a target_structure that differs materially from the one it used in E01/E02, satisfying P4-DR-05.
batch_design_rationale.keyword_freshness: No keyword in this batch has been used in E01 or E02, and no keyword is repeated between E03 and E04, satisfying P4-DR-03 and P4-DR-06.
batch_design_rationale.blind_solve_learning_applied: The E01 Part 2 teacher patch recorded four open-cloze items where a second answer stayed defensible (if/when, was/is, best/how, in/for). That finding belongs to the open-cloze construct, not to Part 4, but the same principle is applied here through P4-DR-13: every slot's `avoid` block now names the specific competing route that must be closed at generation, rather than leaving uniqueness to be discovered after the item exists.

slots.target_structure: negative equivalence with not as … as
slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve a comparative relation between two items by reversing which one is the subject, without changing which is greater.
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: AS + correct gradable adjective; MP2: second AS introducing the standard of comparison
avoid: Do not choose an adjective that also permits a natural 'less … than' answer, since sentence2 must be uniquely solvable.
Do not select an adjective with an irregular or contested comparative form.
Do not allow the answer to be recoverable without reversing the subjects.
Do not reuse the comparative + THAN mechanism already tested at E01 Q27.
history_notes: TF-01 used once at E01 Q27 with target 'comparative equivalence with THAN' and keyword THAN. Target structure and keyword both changed.

slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve a real-time conditional relation while converting a negative if-clause into a single-word negative conditional.
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: UNLESS + subject; MP2: affirmative verb form required by the polarity change
avoid: Do not write sentence1 so that 'if … not' would fit sentence2 equally well; the keyword must be structurally necessary.
Do not leave the verb negative in the answer, which is the commonest wrong route.
Do not use a context where 'otherwise' or 'without' would also complete sentence2 naturally.
Do not reuse the third-conditional mechanism already tested at E01 Q25.
history_notes: TF-02 used once at E01 Q25 with target 'third conditional / unreal past consequence' and keyword HAD. Time reference, target structure and keyword all changed.

slots.target_structure: reported advice with ADVISED + object + to-infinitive
slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve the speech act of advising and the propositional content of the advice given.
slots.answer_shape: ADVISED + object pronoun + TO + base verb
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: ADVISED + object; MP2: TO-infinitive carrying the advised action
avoid: Do not write sentence1 so that 'suggested' or 'recommended' would be the natural report, since those verbs take a different pattern.
Do not make the direct speech an instruction or order, which would point to 'told'.
Do not allow the object to be omissible; ADVISED must require one here.
Do not reuse the reported-request mechanism already tested at E01 Q28.
history_notes: TF-05 used once at E01 Q28 with target 'reported request / ask someone to' and keyword ASKED. Speech act changed from request to advice; keyword changed.

slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve the meaning that an action was hard for the subject, moving from an adjective frame to a noun-plus-gerund complement.
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: correctly tensed form of HAVE + DIFFICULTY; MP2: gerund carrying the action
avoid: Do not allow 'trouble' or 'problems' to fit, since the keyword is fixed but sentence1 must not simply signal a synonym swap.
Do not write sentence1 so that a to-infinitive complement would read naturally after DIFFICULTY.
Do not leave the tense of HAVE recoverable from more than one reading of sentence1.
Accept 'difficulty in + gerund' as a controlled variant, mapping to the same two marking points, provided the total stays within five words.
Do not reuse the 'there is no point in + gerund' mechanism already tested at E01 Q29.
history_notes: TF-09 used once at E01 Q29 with target 'there is no point in + gerund' and keyword POINT. Both are noun-plus-gerund frames, so the generation prompt must keep the sentence contexts clearly unrelated.

slots.target_structure: be responsible for + noun phrase or gerund
slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve the attribution of duty or cause, moving from a plain verb to an adjective-plus-dependent-preposition frame.
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: correctly tensed BE + RESPONSIBLE; MP2: dependent preposition FOR introducing the complement
avoid: Do not write sentence1 so that 'in charge of' or 'responsible to' could be read as equally correct.
Do not make the tense of BE ambiguous between present and past.
Do not choose a context where blame rather than duty is meant, unless sentence1 makes that unambiguous.
Do not reuse the 'accuse someone of' mechanism already tested at E01 Q30.
history_notes: TF-12 used once at E01 Q30 with target 'accuse someone of + gerund/noun' and keyword ACCUSED. Lexical head and preposition both changed.

slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve a polite request for help by replacing a direct request with a fixed idiomatic chunk.
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: DO + indirect object; MP2: determiner A + FAVOUR as a fixed chunk
avoid: Do not permit 'do a favour for me', which changes the pattern and the word count; sentence2 must force the ditransitive order.
Do not allow the determiner to be droppable.
Do not choose a context where 'help me out' would fit sentence2 without the keyword.
Use the British spelling FAVOUR throughout; FAVOR must not be accepted as a variant.
history_notes: TF-11 is untested. Blueprint System v1.0 §10 requires it to be prioritised in this batch. First scored use in the system.

example_slot_guidance.suggested_source: Draw the example from TF-08 or TF-13, both of which are rested from the scored slots in this batch, and from a keyword unused in E01/E02.

slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve the meaning of disposing of or removing something, replacing a single lexical verb with a fixed three-part multi-word verb.
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: correctly tensed GET + RID; MP2: preposition OF introducing the object
avoid: Do not make the tense of GET recoverable in more than one way from sentence1.
Do not choose an object that makes 'throw away' the only natural reading, since the two are not always interchangeable.
Do not allow 'be rid of', which is a different structure with a different meaning.
Do not reuse the 'make up one's mind' mechanism already tested at E02 Q29.
history_notes: TF-10 used once at E02 Q29 with target 'make up one's mind / decision equivalence' and keyword MIND. Verb and keyword both changed.

slots.target_structure: must have + past participle for deduction about the past
slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve a confident deduction about a completed past event, converting an explicit statement of certainty into modal-perfect form.
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: MUST HAVE; MP2: past participle carrying the deduced event
avoid: Do not write sentence1 so that 'might have' or 'could have' would preserve the meaning; the certainty must be explicit.
Do not allow a negative deduction reading, which would point to 'can't have'.
Do not use an obligation context, which would make MUST a different modal altogether.
Do not reuse the 'need not have' mechanism already tested at E02 Q27.
history_notes: TF-06 used once at E02 Q27 with target 'need not have + past participle' and keyword NEED. Modal meaning changed from unnecessary-but-done to past deduction; keyword changed.

slots.target_structure: this is the first time + present perfect
slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve the meaning that an experience has never happened before, converting a negative present-perfect statement into a first-time frame.
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: FIRST TIME as the fixed frame; MP2: subject + present-perfect verb form
avoid: Do not allow a past-simple continuation, which is the commonest wrong route.
Do not write sentence1 so that 'the first time' could refer to a specific past occasion rather than the present one.
Accept the contracted present perfect ('I've') as a controlled variant mapping to the same two marking points; the uncontracted form must also fit inside five words.
Do not reuse the 'time since + past simple' mechanism already tested at E02 Q28.
history_notes: TF-07 used once at E02 Q28 with target 'time since + past simple ↔ present-perfect duration' and keyword SINCE. Both involve the present perfect, so the generation prompt must avoid any duration reading here.

slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve a speaker's preference about somebody else's behaviour, converting a direct request or preference into the unreal-past would-rather pattern.
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: WOULD RATHER + subject; MP2: past-simple verb form required by the second-subject pattern
avoid: Do not write sentence1 so that a to-infinitive continuation ('would rather not do it') would fit; the preference must concern another person.
Do not allow a present-simple verb after the second subject, which is the commonest wrong route.
Do not use a context where 'would prefer you to' fits sentence2 equally naturally.
Do not reuse the 'wish + past perfect' mechanism already tested at E02 Q25.
history_notes: TF-03 used once at E02 Q25 with target 'wish + past perfect' and keyword WISH. Regret about the past changed to preference about another person's present behaviour; keyword changed.

slots.target_structure: adjective clause recast as a definite noun phrase: how deep it is → the depth of it
slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve the same proposition while replacing an embedded wh-clause with a nominalised measurement phrase.
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: definite article + DEPTH as the nominalised head; MP2: preposition OF linking the noun phrase to its complement
avoid: Do not leave the wh-clause recoverable, since the transformation must be structural rather than lexical.
Do not choose a noun whose derived form is irregular or above B2.
Do not allow 'how deep' to remain grammatical in sentence2.
Do not write sentence1 so that a possessive ('its depth') would fit sentence2, since that changes the word count and the marking points.
history_notes: TF-14 is untested. Blueprint System v1.0 §10 requires it to be prioritised in this batch. First scored use in the system.

slots.target_structure: impersonal reporting with be thought to have + past participle
slots.semantic_equivalence_goal: Preserve an attributed general belief about a completed past event, converting 'people think that …' into a personal passive with a perfect infinitive.
slots.answer_shape: BE (present) + THOUGHT + TO HAVE + past participle
slots.marking_point_plan: MP1: passive BE + THOUGHT; MP2: TO HAVE + past participle carrying the completed event
avoid: Do not allow a simple infinitive ('to cause'), which would lose the past reference; sentence1 must place the event clearly in the past.
Do not allow the anticipatory 'it is thought that' route to fit sentence2; the subject must already be raised.
Do not make the tense of BE ambiguous; the belief must be current.
Do not reuse the 'be expected to + infinitive' mechanism already tested at E02 Q26, which has no perfect infinitive.
history_notes: TF-04 used once at E02 Q26 with target 'subject + be EXPECTED + to-infinitive' and keyword EXPECTED. The perfect infinitive and the past reference are what distinguish this slot; flagged for reviewer attention because both are raised-subject passives.
